Tag input

A box holding the values already added, as removable tags, and a text input for adding the next one.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For several short values of the same kind that the reader types: labels on a task, reviewers, paths an agent may change.
  • When the values are free text, or come from a list too long to show as checkboxes.

When not to use it

  • For one value. Use a field, or a combobox when it comes from a list.
  • For a few known options. Use checkboxes.
  • To show the filters in force on a list. Use tags in a row above the list, with no input.
  • For long values, such as sentences. Use a textarea, one value to a line.

Sizes

default
As wide as the field and 54px tall with one row. The box grows as tags wrap.

Accessibility

  • Inside ds-field, after the label, put a div with ds-tag-input. It holds a ul with ds-tag-input__tags and an aria-label that says what the values are, such as Labels added, then an input type="text" with ds-tag-input__input. The label's for attribute matches the input's id.
  • Each value is an li with the class ds-tag holding its text and a button with ds-tag__remove, copied from the tag component. The button's aria-label names the value: Remove label: backend. Keep the ul in the markup when it is empty.
  • Say which key adds a value in a ds-field__description linked with aria-describedby: Enter always, and a comma only where a value cannot hold one. On a phone, enterkeyhint="done" labels the key.
  • The app wires the keys: on Enter or the separator it trims what was typed, appends an li, empties the input and prevents the form from being sent. A pasted list is split on the separator. Backspace in the empty input removes the last tag. Typing the same value twice adds nothing.
  • After a value is added or removed, say so in a ds-visually-hidden element with role="status", such as backend added, 3 labels. After a remove button is pressed, move focus to the next tag's button, or to the input when none is left.
  • For a value that cannot be added, leave it in the input, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a ds-field__error that repeats the value and says what to type. The box's border turns to the danger colour and the error's icon marks it as well.
  • Send the values with the form as one hidden input per value, or as the app's own state. The text input holds only the value being typed.
  • Tab reaches each remove button and then the input. Set disabled on the input and on every remove button when the values cannot change.
